stem: A 7-year-old child presents with brief episodes of behavioral arrest and lip smacking. If the EEG shows a typical $3\text{ Hz}$ spike and wave pattern, what is the drug of choice if no other seizure types are present?
explanation: Ethosuximide is the first-line drug of choice for pure childhood absence epilepsy without generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
rationale: Look for the specific medication that is the primary treatment for childhood absence epilepsy.

optionExplanations.A: While effective, this is generally reserved as a second-line option if the primary drug fails or if tonic-clonic seizures are also present.
optionExplanations.B: This sodium channel blocker can actually worsen absence seizures and is not indicated for this syndrome.
optionExplanations.C: Ethosuximide is the first-line drug of choice for pure childhood absence epilepsy without generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
optionExplanations.D: Though a broad-spectrum medication, it is not the gold-standard first-line treatment for typical absence seizures.
